title: Greg Doucette's MainGaining is keeping you small?! (Analyzing Revival Fitness Ex
summary: Responding to Revival Fitness's two-hour video, NH argues that the problem is not the practice of a lean bulk or recomp but the word 'maingaining', which Greg Doucette keeps redefining, confusing beginners into recomping when they are skinny. He also warns Revival's audience not to swing into the opposite 'bulking meme', stresses that performance is not aesthetics, and insists on personal responsibility and critical thinking.
claims: When NH says maingaining he means a lean bulk; calling a recomp 'gaining' makes no sense because bodyweight stays the same
Maingaining is a made-up word that Greg Doucette redefines at will, anywhere from maintenance to a +300 kcal surplus, so he can always be right and take credit for any subscriber's progress
A big YouTuber who is beginners' first source of information acts as a gatekeeper and carries extra responsibility for teaching in simple, consistent terms

Beginners told to 'maingain' end up doing different things (recomp, lean bulk, deficit), like a program with an exercise that could mean anything; the term should be dropped and replaced with 'lean bulk' or 'recomp'
Don't reject correct ideas just because Greg promotes them, e.g. calories in, calories out is simplistic but chemically correct
Greg's anti-fat messaging pushes his subscribers to interpret maingaining as maintenance, so skinny beginners recomp and never grow
Greg's views on gaining are skewed by PED use: gaining lots of muscle at maintenance or a tiny surplus works on drugs, not for naturals
For skinny naturals the way forward is a lean bulk
NH's best gains came from a very small, consistent calorie surplus held over years
'Ab anxiety': people cling to a six-pack and never raise bodyweight; adding weight raises total fat but not necessarily bodyfat percentage if muscle is gained at the same time
For a skinny man, muscle combined with some fat is what transforms the look; most admired naturals carry a fair amount of fat
NH estimates himself at 16-17% bodyfat and says it makes him look good
Nobody can eyeball bodyfat percentage accurately and knowing it is almost useless; how you look and feel is what matters
NH has been recomping for two years without knowing his bodyfat; he simply reached a mass he was comfortable with and wanted to refine it
A recomp is valid if you already have muscle and enough bodyfat; if you are skinny you have nothing to recomp and shouldn't do it
Being fat is terrible for health and you should get to a lower bodyfat as soon as possible, without a suicide cut
Pudgy beginners are the ones who could have benefited from recomping, but maingaining marketing targets skinny novices
People who wasted years maingaining share the blame: if you saw no strength or muscle progress for months and never questioned it, you need to take personal responsibility
Gaining muscle on maintenance or a deficit when you weigh 130 lb is a meme you should have seen through
Revival's audience risks falling for a second meme, blind bulking; only do something if you understand it and it fits your goals
Fitness culture swings like a pendulum; after the anti-maingaining shift we must avoid swinging into people stuffing their faces and getting fat
Some people can gain muscle at 12-13% bodyfat; Revival's preferred range is skewed too high, and the right level depends on your preferences
Choose how lean or bulky to be according to your own goals, not your favorite YouTuber's
Performance and muscle gain are not one-to-one: scale weight and weight on the bar going up does not mean muscle is being built
You don't need to eat big to get big; do a slow lean bulk and control fat gain
Alpha Destiny and Bugenhagen gain mass to chase PRs; performance requires mass, not necessarily muscle, so their examples do not prove that you must dirty bulk to be lean and muscular
NH built 70-80 lb of mass going from about 110 to about 180-190 lb on a lean bulk without ever being chubby
NH later got fat eating too much, reaching 240 lb; he considers those years wasted and cutting back was hard
Using enhanced pro bodybuilders like Chris Bumstead as examples for natural dieting is invalid, whether it is Greg or Revival doing it
Explain why something works instead of relying on 'this famous guy does it' as social proof
Greg tells subscribers their lack of progress is due to bad genetics, a black pill that removes responsibility and keeps them small and dependent
The only way out of maingaining is to enter a surplus, gain mass and see for yourself; always try things, even against your favorite YouTuber
Beware of a savior complex: being rescued from Greg by Revival doesn't mean Revival knows what's best for you
